title: Weakness Localization Is Not Enough: State-Aware Recursive Knowledge Improvement for Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.36811v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Knowledge improvement in large language models is shifting from predefined knowledge incorporation pipelines toward evaluation-guided updating. Existing methods use evaluation to localize model-specific knowledge weaknesses and guide targeted post-training. However, identifying what to improve does not necessarily provide sufficient information for deciding how to improve it. The same localized weakness can be compatible with distinct operational knowledge states: the relevant knowledge may be unavailable, available but difficult to access reliably, or accessible but ineffective for downstream use. We call this ambiguity knowledge-state aliasing. When compatible states favor different interventions, greater diagnostic resolution alone is insufficient for intervention selection. translated_title: 弱点定位并不足够：面向大语言模型的状态感知递归知识改进
translated_abstract: 大语言模型的知识改进正从预定义的知识注入流程转向评估引导的更新。现有方法利用评估来定位模型特有的知识弱点，并据此指导有针对性的后训练。然而，识别“需要改进什么”并不一定能为决定“如何改进”提供充分的信息。同一个被定位出的弱点可能与多种不同的操作性知识状态相容：相关知识可能不可用、可用但难以可靠访问，或可访问但在下游使用中无效。我们将这种歧义称为“知识状态混叠”。当相容的知识状态倾向于不同的干预措施时，仅靠更高的诊断分辨率并不足以选择合适的干预方式。此外，模型更新可能在观察到的弱点消失之前就已改变底层知识状态，因此某一轮中合适的干预措施在后续轮次中可能不再适用……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文指出仅定位模型知识弱点不足以决定如何改进（存在“知识状态混叠”问题），并提出状态感知的递归知识改进方法，根据知识是缺失、难以访问还是下游无效等不同状态选择相应的干预策略。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that localizing knowledge weaknesses is insufficient for deciding how to improve them due to "knowledge-state aliasing," and proposes a state-aware recursive knowledge improvement approach that selects interventions according to whether knowledge is unavailable, hard to access reliably, or ineffective for downstream use.
